paragraphs.english: A walking club planned a trip along a forest path. The leader, Sam, knew the route well and thought everyone could finish it in two hours. On the first practice walk, however, the group soon spread out. Some members stopped to take pictures, while others walked slowly on the steep parts. The fastest members reached the end without seeing the rest of the group for almost an hour. Sam realized that knowing a path was not the same as planning a good group trip. Before the next walk, he asked members about their pace and interests. He marked three meeting points and chose someone to walk at the back. The group also agreed on a signal for asking for a rest. The second walk took longer, but everyone reached the end together and shared what they had noticed. Sam learned that a successful trip should be measured by the group's experience, not just by the time on his own watch.
paragraphs.translation: ウォーキングクラブは、森の道を歩く旅行を計画した。リーダーのサムは道をよく知り、全員二時間で終えられると思った。しかし最初の練習では、集団はすぐばらばらになった。写真を撮るために止まる人も、急な場所をゆっくり歩く人もいた。最も速い人たちは、ほぼ一時間ほかの仲間に会わないまま終点へ着いた。道を知ることと、よい団体旅行を計画することは同じでないとサムは気づいた。次の散歩前に、仲間の速さと興味を尋ねた。集合地点を三か所示し、最後尾を歩く人を選んだ。グループは、休憩を頼む合図も決めた。二回目は時間が長くかかったが、全員一緒に着き、気づいたことを共有した。成功した旅行は、自分の時計の時間だけでなく、集団の体験で測るべきだと学んだ。

paragraphs.english: A community center invited local families to a free music evening. The staff posted a colorful invitation on social media and expected a large audience. Only twelve people came. At first, the manager thought families were not interested in music. A volunteer named Amy asked visitors at the center how they usually learned about events. Some checked social media every day, but others read the board at the bus stop or looked for notices in their children's school bags. A few people did not know that the center's social media page existed. For the next music evening, the staff used several ways to share the same information. They put paper notices in shops and asked the school to include a short message in its newsletter. More families attended, including several who had missed the first invitation. Amy explained that a message could be attractive and correct but still fail if it never reached the people who needed to see it.
paragraphs.translation: 地域センターは、無料の音楽の夕べに近所の家族を招いた。職員はSNSに色鮮やかな案内を載せ、大勢の観客を期待した。来たのは十二人だけだった。当初、管理者は家族が音楽に興味を持っていないと思った。エイミーというボランティアは、来館者に普段どう行事を知るか尋ねた。毎日SNSを見る人もいたが、バス停の掲示板や、子供の通学かばんに入ったお知らせを見る人もいた。センターのSNSページの存在を知らない人もいた。次の音楽会では、同じ情報を複数の方法で届けた。店に紙の案内を置き、学校には通信に短い案内を載せてもらうよう頼んだ。前回の招待を見逃した人も含め、より多くの家族が参加した。案内が魅力的で正確でも、必要な人に届かなければうまくいかないとエイミーは説明した。

paragraphs.english: Mia saved money to buy a small desk lamp. At a shop, she found two lamps that looked almost the same. One was cheaper, so she was ready to buy it. Her father asked her to read the information on both boxes first. The cheaper lamp needed a special kind of battery that the shop did not sell. The other could use ordinary batteries or connect to a wall socket. Mia also checked whether a broken part could be replaced and how long the shop would accept returns. She did not simply choose the more expensive lamp because her father mentioned it. Instead, she wrote down the costs and features that mattered to her. In the end, she chose the second lamp because she planned to use it at her desk every evening. The experience taught her that a price label was only one part of a buying decision. Asking the right questions helped her spend her savings more carefully.
paragraphs.translation: ミアは小さな電気スタンドを買うため貯金した。店で、ほとんど同じに見える二つのスタンドを見つけた。一方が安かったので、それを買おうとしていた。父親は、先に両方の箱の情報を読むよう頼んだ。安い方には、その店では売っていない特殊な電池が必要だった。もう一方は普通の電池を使うか、壁のコンセントへつなげられた。壊れた部品を交換できるか、店がいつまで返品を受け付けるかも調べた。父親が言及したからというだけで、高い方を選んだのではなかった。代わりに、自分に重要な費用と機能を書き出した。結局、毎晩机で使う予定だったので、二つ目のスタンドを選んだ。この体験から、値札は購入判断の一部分にすぎないと学んだ。適切な質問が、貯金をより慎重に使う助けになった。

paragraphs.english: The photography club held a meeting where each member showed one picture. Most students brought their best work. Alex brought a photograph that was too dark. Some members wondered why he had chosen it. Alex explained that he liked the shape of the trees but had used the wrong camera setting. He wanted advice about taking the same scene again. The discussion became more lively than usual. One student suggested a different time of day, and another showed how to change a setting. Soon other members began sharing pictures that had not turned out well. The club adviser said that showing success could encourage people, but showing an unfinished attempt could invite useful help. The following month, the club added a short session called Work in Progress. Members still celebrated their best pictures, but they no longer felt that every meeting had to be a competition. Alex returned to the trees and took a clearer photograph with ideas he had learned from his friends.
paragraphs.translation: 写真部は、各部員が一枚見せる会合を開いた。大半の生徒は最もよい作品を持ってきた。アレックスは暗すぎる写真を持ってきた。なぜその写真を選んだのか、不思議に思う部員もいた。木々の形は好きだったが、カメラの設定を間違えたと説明した。同じ景色を撮り直す助言が欲しかった。話し合いは普段より活発になった。一人が違う時間帯を提案し、別の一人が設定の変え方を示した。やがて他の部員も、うまく撮れなかった写真を見せ始めた。顧問は、成功例で人を励ませるが、未完成の試みを見せれば有用な助けを得られると話した。翌月、部は「制作途中」と呼ぶ短い時間を加えた。最良の写真を祝い続けたが、毎回が競争でなければならないとは思わなくなった。アレックスは木々の所へ戻り、友人から学んだ考えを使って、より鮮明な写真を撮った。

paragraphs.english: Two schools in different towns started an online book club. The teachers chose the same short novel for both groups. At the first meeting, students tried to discuss the whole book at once. The conversation moved quickly, and several students who had read carefully said very little. For the second meeting, the teachers asked each group to bring one question and one favorite passage. They sent these to the other school two days before the call. Students had time to think and look at the book again. During the meeting, they discovered that they understood one character's choice differently. Instead of arguing about who was right, they pointed to words in the story and explained their reasons. The meeting ended with more questions than it had started with, but everyone wanted to read the next book. The teachers were happy because the club had become a place for careful conversation rather than a test of who could answer fastest.
paragraphs.translation: 別の町の二校が、オンライン読書クラブを始めた。先生たちは両方のグループに同じ短い小説を選んだ。最初の会では、本全体を一度に議論しようとした。話は速く進み、よく読んでいた何人かの生徒もほとんど発言しなかった。二回目には、先生は各グループに質問一つと好きな一節を持ち寄るよう頼んだ。通話の二日前に、それらを相手校へ送った。生徒は考えたり本を読み返したりする時間を得た。会合中、一人の登場人物の選択を違って理解していると分かった。どちらが正しいか争わず、物語の言葉を示して理由を説明した。開始時より多くの問いを残して会は終わったが、皆は次の本を読みたがった。読書会が早答えの競争ではなく、丁寧に話し合う場になったので、先生たちは喜んだ。

sentences.translation: 読書会が早答えの競争ではなく、丁寧に話し合う場になったので、先生たちは喜んだ。

exerciseParagraphs.english: Two schools in different towns started an online book club. The teachers chose the same short novel for both groups. At the first meeting, students tried to discuss the whole book at once. The conversation moved quickly, and several students who had read carefully said very little.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: 別の町の二校が、オンライン読書クラブを始めた。先生たちは両方のグループに同じ短い小説を選んだ。最初の会では、本全体を一度に議論しようとした。話は速く進み、よく読んでいた何人かの生徒もほとんど発言しなかった。

exerciseParagraphs.english: For the second meeting, the teachers asked each group to bring one question and one favorite passage. They sent these to the other school two days before the call. Students had time to think and look at the book again.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: 二回目には、先生は各グループに質問一つと好きな一節を持ち寄るよう頼んだ。通話の二日前に、それらを相手校へ送った。生徒は考えたり本を読み返したりする時間を得た。

exerciseParagraphs.english: During the meeting, they discovered that they understood one character's choice differently. Instead of arguing about who was right, they pointed to words in the story and explained their reasons.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: 会合中、一人の登場人物の選択を違って理解していると分かった。どちらが正しいか争わず、物語の言葉を示して理由を説明した。

exerciseParagraphs.english: The meeting ended with more questions than it had started with, but everyone wanted to read the next book. The teachers were happy because the club had become a place for careful conversation rather than a test of who could answer fastest.
exerciseParagraphs.translation: 開始時より多くの問いを残して会は終わったが、皆は次の本を読みたがった。読書会が早答えの競争ではなく、丁寧に話し合う場になったので、先生たちは喜んだ。
